findings.reason: Verified that the user-storage success branch returns without deleting any local recovery-codes credential, and that isValid falls through to the local validator when the federated one rejects, so a stale local code can still log in; the scenario is real but narrow (a federated user with pre-existing local codes who regenerates).

Verified that the authenticator's allCodesUsed cleanup calls removeStoredCredentialById, which goes to the local store, and that the test provider's isValid never removes a used code, so the federated code can be reused; the consumption contract is left to providers, which limits severity.

Confirmed the default CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials returns an empty stream and that the new override now returns OTP, which weakens legacy-path coverage, but this is a test-provider coverage and design concern rather than a product defect.

Confirmed createFromValues never sets an id and that disable/disableable lists ignore recovery codes, but the defect is confined to the test-only compatibility provider; the null-user NPE is unlikely since the user was loaded through this provider.
The test only logs in once with code 0, so it cannot catch reuse or the next-code check; this is a valid gap tied to finding 1, though it is not on a critical path, and the alias typo is trivial.

The hard-coded id equals the constant in the services module, and the suggestion is hedged on whether the module can see it; the failure requires the constant to change, so this is a marginal cleanup.
